(2019) showed empirically produce better loss basin escape in SGD than Gaussian noise of equivalent variance. For Pareto front coverage specifically, sustained conflict keeps the policy in a high-gradient-angle regime continuously, which means the projection mechanism is always active and always contracting the effective step — the policy explores the conflict zone but never settles long enough to accurately estimate whether it has reached a true front point or merely a high-conflict interior region. Bursty conflict, by contrast, allows the policy to drift under low-conflict conditions toward a local attractor (potentially a true front point), then receive a large displacement event that kicks it into a new basin — this is structurally identical to the iterated local search metaheuristic, which has provable advantages over continuous perturbation for non-convex multimodal landscapes when burst magnitude exceeds the local basin radius. The practical evidence appears in curriculum learning dynamics: Graves et al.
